extracted.intended_audience: utilities (pole owners), prospective attachers (broadband providers/WISPs/etc.), and legal/practice stakeholders participating in FCC pole-attachment rulemaking and compliance
extracted.subtask_description: FCC Fourth Report and Order / Further Notice guidance and proposed rules governing pole attachments, make-ready timelines, cost allocation, contractor use, and easement information, intended to direct utilities and attachers and to solicit comment on specific rule changes for large orders and self-help practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-causation and cost-allocation under §1.1408(b) ('necessitated solely')
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1.1408(b) must be read to mean that parties benefitting from a modification share proportionately in its costs, unless a modification is 'necessitated solely' by an additional or modified attachment of another party, in which case that party bears the costs of the modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to pole replacements, a utility may not require a new attacher to pay the entire cost of a pole replacement when the pole already requires replacement at the time of the attachment request. The Commission follows precedent (e.g., 2021 Pole Replacement Declaratory Ruling and 1996 Local Competition Order) that distinguishes modifications necessitated solely by a new attachment from those already planned or necessary for other reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of poles already scheduled/identified for replacement ('red tagged')
rubrics_metrics.description: If a pole has been designated for replacement at the time of a pole attachment application (e.g., identified in inspection as not safe/serviceable or unlikely to remain so for the next inspection cycle), the subsequent new attachment request does not 'solely necessitate' that replacement; the utility bears the replacement cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission declined to adopt various mechanical examples (unsalvageable, fully depreciated, older than 30 years) as definitive tests. Determinations should be grounded in inspections and safety/serviceability standards (e.g., NESC inspection cycles), and parties opposed adding potentially confusing bright-line examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attacher responsibility limited to incremental pole upgrade costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A prospective attacher is responsible for the incremental cost associated with needing a taller or stronger pole to support its facilities, but not for the cost to replace a defective or deteriorated pole with an equivalent-sized pole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilities may charge a new attacher for incremental make-ready costs specifically attributable to installing a stronger/heavier/taller pole if the utility sufficiently documents those incremental make-ready costs. The base replacement cost for a deteriorated pole identified for replacement is borne by the utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: No attacher self-help remedies for pole replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no attacher self-help remedies available for pole replacements under current rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where self-help exists for surveys and make-ready in certain circumstances, pole replacement is excluded from attacher self-help remedies (see 47 CFR § 1.1411(i)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-of-way and easement information disclosure requirement (section 224(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities must provide potential attachers with a copy of the utility's easement (rights-of-way) related to property where poles covered by an attachment application are located before a utility can refuse to let the attacher share that easement or require the attacher to obtain its own easement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is required to enable attachers to evaluate the scope of the utility's easement under state law where the utility claims the easement cannot accommodate an attacher. The requirement does not compel utilities to alter easements or act contrary to state law; it requires sharing of information about the easement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard make-ready timelines and numeric thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications-space make-ready must be completed within 30 days after the utility notifies all existing attachers on a pole for requests up to the lesser of 300 poles or 0.5% of the utility's poles in a state; that timeframe is extended by 45 days for requests up to the lesser of 3,000 poles or 5% of the utility's poles in a state; requests exceeding that threshold are subject to negotiation in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule provides 90 days for make-ready above the communications space. The Commission clarifies that for very large orders the first 3,000 poles (or 5%) are subject to the §1.1411(g)(3) timeline and encourages coordinated designation by attachers of which poles will be processed first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative approach for very large orders: additional make-ready time (proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission tentatively concludes utilities should have an additional 90 days for make-ready for requests exceeding 3,000 poles or 5% of a utility's poles in a state, and seeks comment on this tentative conclusion and on alternative tiered timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission solicits comment on whether 90 additional days is sufficient, whether other amounts or additional tiers per increment (e.g., per 3,000 poles) are appropriate, and whether existing flexibility provisions suffice. The Commission recognizes operational constraints (permitting, workforce, coordination) that may affect feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility obligation to negotiate make-ready timing in good faith (§1.1411(g)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the rules require negotiation in good faith for make-ready timelines (e.g., for very large orders), a utility's obligation to 'negotiate in good faith' implies an obligation to exercise reasonable efforts to accommodate attachment needs and not indefinitely delay or refuse to provide make-ready timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission expects utilities to engage constructively and not use indefinite delay as a tactic. The scope of good faith negotiation may vary with application size and facts; the record is insufficient to adopt fixed timelines for all large orders now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on utilities limiting application size/number to avoid timelines (proposal for comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCTA proposed revising rules to prohibit utilities from imposing limits on the number of poles per application or number of concurrent applications so as to avoid make-ready timelines; the Commission seeks comment on prevalence and effects of such utility-imposed limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission asks whether prohibiting such limits would speed attachment processing or whether legitimate operational reasons (workforce, permitting, coordination) justify limits; commenters should provide evidence on prevalence and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-help acceleration proposals (15-day notification proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCTA proposes that utilities notify attachers within 15 days after receiving a complete application if the utility cannot conduct the survey within the required 45-day period, allowing the attacher to elect self-help sooner; NCTA also proposes making self-help available for the estimate process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission declined to adopt these changes in the Fourth Report and Order pending a fuller record but seeks comment on feasibility: whether utilities can reliably notify within 15 business days and whether enough qualified contractors exist to make this effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attacher use of contractors and utility contractor-list obligations (§§1.1411(i)-(j), 1.1412)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachers may perform self-help surveys and make-ready (or elect one-touch make-ready) when utilities miss deadlines, but must use utility-approved contractors. For complex make-ready or above communications space work, utilities must maintain a reasonably sufficient, up-to-date list of authorized contractors; for surveys/simple make-ready the utility may but is not required to maintain such a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a utility provides a list, the attacher must choose a contractor from it; attachers may request additions and the utility cannot unreasonably withhold consent. If no list exists or no approved contractor is available within a reasonable time, the attacher may choose its own qualified contractor, subject to limited disqualification by the utility for reasonable safety/reliability concerns and a requirement the utility identify at least one available qualified contractor instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor disqualification standards and utility notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility may disqualify an attacher's chosen contractor only for reasonable safety or reliability concerns related to the contractor's failure to meet the Commission's minimum qualifications or the utility's publicly available, commercially reasonable safety/reliability standards; disqualification must be accompanied by written notice identifying the basis and at least one available qualified contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualification must be prompt, in writing, nondiscriminatory, and based on fair application of commercially reasonable contractor requirements; utilities are required to identify alternatives when they disqualify a contractor for valid reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'complex make-ready'
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex make-ready includes transfers and work within the communications space on a pole that would be reasonably likely to cause a service outage(s) or facility damage, including splicing of any communication attachment or relocation of existing wireless attachments; all wireless activities (mobile, fixed, point-to-point, WISPs) are to be considered complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 47 CFR § 1.1402(p) for the regulatory definition; complex work triggers the requirement that utilities maintain an up-to-date contractor list and other protections for safety and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation parties negotiate in good faith even absent specific rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where there is not a specific Commission rule or policy that governs a particular situation, the Commission expects parties to negotiate in good faith to resolve issues that may arise during attachment and make-ready processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission emphasizes cooperative negotiation to expedite deployment, especially given the anticipated influx of large attachment applications associated with federal broadband funding programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork, RFA, PRA, and comment procedures for rulemaking changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to rules (including 47 CFR §§ 1.1411, 1.1415, 1.1416) may create new or modified information collection requirements subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act and require Regulatory Flexibility Analyses; the Further Notice contains specified comment deadlines and instructions for filing comments and IRFA responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should file comments by the dates listed in the Further Notice and include separate headings for IRFA responses; proposed information collections will be submitted to OMB for review and public comment will be invited.
